title: Many Cultures, One City
text:
Our city has people from many countries. Some families speak Spanish at home, and others speak Arabic or Chinese. In school, children learn about different holidays and foods.

Cultural diversity makes the city more interesting. People can share food, music, and stories with their neighbors. When we learn about other cultures, we understand each other better.

questions.text: What languages do some families speak at home?
What can people share with their neighbors?
What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Learning about other cultures helps people understand each other
Children should not go to school

questions.text: Why does the writer say the city is more interesting?
options: Because people from many cultures live there
Because the city is very old
Because the city is very small

vocabulary.definition: special days when people do not work or go to school
the ways of life of a group of people
having many different kinds of people or things

paragraph_translations: Nuestra ciudad tiene personas de muchos países. Algunas familias hablan español en casa, y otras hablan árabe o chino. En la escuela, los niños aprenden sobre diferentes fiestas y comidas.
La diversidad cultural hace que la ciudad sea más interesante. Las personas pueden compartir comida, música y cuentos con sus vecinos. Cuando aprendemos sobre otras culturas, nos entendemos mejor.
